identity.source_note: Authoritative JBJS Instructions for Authors. The journals.lww.com/jbjsjournal 'Information for Authors' page is only a Cloudflare-gated pointer stub that redirects to the submission service; the real guide lives here on jbjs.org. This page is a JS app whose instruction text is embedded in an in-page JavaScript blob, so the README curl+strip-tags recipe normalizes to a 32-char shell ('jbjs instructions for authors'); the recorded hash is of that shell. Rules were extracted from the in-page JS content plus the JBJS New Submission Checklist PDF (sites.jbjs.org/jbjs/jbjs_author_new_submission_checklist.pdf), the Reference Formatting Guidelines (jbjs.org/reference-guidelines.php), and the Figure Guidelines (jbjs.org/guidelines-figures.php).

encoding_notes: guidelines_url is the authoritative JBJS Instructions for Authors on jbjs.org. The publisher's journals.lww.com/jbjsjournal 'Information for Authors' page is a Cloudflare-gated pointer stub with no formatting rules (it only says submissions go through a submission service); the real rules live on jbjs.org and in Editorial Manager.

source_hash is of the page shell only: jbjs.org/jbjs-ifa.php serves its instruction text inside an in-page JavaScript blob, so the README strip-tags recipe yields a 32-char shell. Rules were read from that JS blob plus the JBJS New Submission Checklist PDF, Reference Formatting Guidelines, and Figure Guidelines. Session C's headless fetch will produce a richer hash.

JBJS article types were mapped onto the shared ARTICLE_TYPES enum: RCT / Observational Study / Basic-Science Study / Survey Study -> original_research (all share a 2500-word limit, structured abstract, and combined <=5 tables-and-figures cap); Evidence-Based Systematic Review -> systematic_review; Expert Review (invited) -> narrative_review; Innovation -> technical_note; Viewpoint -> editorial; Correspondence (eLetters) -> letter.

JBJS article types with no clean enum slot were omitted: Health Care Recommendation (guideline/consensus), Patient Voices, Arts and Humanities, Ethics essay, and World Report (invited regional report).

figures_max / tables_max encode the journal's stated cap as an upper bound per field, but JBJS actually specifies a COMBINED limit: <=5 tables-and-figures TOTAL for 2500-word scientific/review types and <=3 total for 1500-word Innovation/Viewpoint/Ethics types. The schema has no combined field; the engine should treat these as a shared budget, not independent maxima.

Blinding: double-blind review is done in-house. The New Submission Checklist states 'Manuscript is free of blinding. All blinding will be done in-house by the Editorial Department' and authors upload an UNBLINDED separate title page plus an unblinded manuscript as individual Word files. Hence scrub_body_identifiers and scrub_metadata are false (author does not blind), while separate_title_page is true and double_blind is true.

Abstract: structured, 5 paragraphs, <=325 words (Background / Methods / Results / Conclusions / Level of Evidence or Clinical Relevance); the cap rises to 350 words for clinical studies that report summary race/ethnicity demographics. Some article types instead require a bulleted abstract (3-5 takeaways) or no abstract (e.g. Ethics uses a brief clinical scenario) — captured as abstract_max_words null for those types.

Layout font/spacing/line-numbering are guide-stated (New Submission Checklist: '12 pt. Times New Roman or Calibri, double-spaced, with continuous line numbering'); Calibri 12 is an allowed alternative to Times New Roman not representable in the single-font schema. page_numbers.show and running_head.show set false because the guide specifies line numbering but not page numbers or a running head; page_size, margins, alignment, first_line_indent, and heading styles are not stated (null).

references.style nlm and journal_abbrev nlm are guide-stated (PubMed/Index Medicus format; all authors listed with no 'et al.' so et_al_threshold is null; numbered by order of citation so order is 'cited'). include_doi is false — the Reference Formatting Guidelines explicitly state 'JBJS does not require DOIs or epub dates.' in_text 'superscript' reflects JBJS published house style; the guide states citation numbering/order but not the in-text marker glyph, so treat in_text as unverified.

Figures: TIFF or EPS only ('No JPG, no figures inserted into Word'); files named by figure number (e.g. Figure1.tif, Figure2.eps) -> naming_pattern 'Figure{n}'; legends placed at end of the manuscript after References -> figure_legends_section. min_dpi 300 is the base (color/halftone at 300 ppi); line art requires up to 1200 ppi, not representable here.

Tables are uploaded as individual Word/Excel files (not embedded), numbered arabic with a descriptive title -> placement separate_file; title above/below not explicitly stated (caption_position null).

misc.orcid_required true: every author must register with ORCID and include the identifier; submission is impossible without an ORCID per author. cover_letter_required false: a cover letter is only conditionally requested (e.g. to note previously reported methodology). Manuscript word count 'includes the abstract but excludes references and figure legends' (New Submission Checklist).
keywords not required: the JBJS Instructions for Authors do not specify manuscript keywords (they may be entered as Editorial Manager metadata). issn and title_case not stated (null).

2026-07-22 et-al doctrine audit: et_al_threshold null -> 'all' — this guide EXPLICITLY requires every author to be listed (statement quoted in the notes above); null now means guide-silent and falls back to the citation style's default.

2026-07-25 Janine LIVE-GUIDE VERIFICATION (jbjs.org/jbjs-ifa.php, read via a browser session — WebFetch returns only the page shell because the instructions load from a JS blob). This file was archive/JS-blob-sourced; it is now live-verified and AUDITS CLEAN. Confirmed verbatim: 2500-word limit + structured abstract for RCT / Observational / Basic-Science / Survey / EBSR; 1500-word limit for Innovation-family types; Expert Review "3000-word limit ... Bulleted abstract" (so narrative_review.abstract_max_words=null is exactly right); abstract "5 paragraphs, totaling no more than 325 words, with the headings: Background ..., Methods, Results, Conclusions, and Level of Evidence or Clinical Relevance"; references "in PubMed/Index Medicus format", "Number the references according to the order of citation in the text (not alphabetically)"; figures "in TIFF or EPS format"; figure legends "at the end of the manuscript text file, after the References section"; tables "in Word or Excel format". CASE REPORTS AND CASE SERIES ARE NOT AN ACCEPTED TYPE - the existing article_types correctly excludes them.

2026-07-25 Janine: references.et_al_threshold='all' CONFIRMED against the live guide - "journal citations must include all authors (not 'et al.') and complete page numbers (not just the first page), per journal style." Session 98's flip was correct.

2026-07-25 Janine: TWO items the live guide adds that this file does not carry, both flagged rather than silently encoded. (1) The 325-word abstract cap has a stated exception - "the word limit is increased to 350 words for articles that include summary demographic information" - which the schema cannot express as a conditional; 325 is the correct base. (2) Expert Review (mapped to narrative_review) is "By invitation only", as is World Report; article_types is about what the journal publishes, not about who may submit, so the type is retained - but an uninvited author formatting an Expert Review for JBJS is told nothing about this. Flagged to Sushant as a UI/report affordance, not a rule change.

2026-07-25 Janine: the COMBINED figure+table cap noted above is now confirmed against the live guide ("<=5 tables and/or figures total", "<=3 tables and/or figures total"). NOT changed this session, deliberately: this file encodes the combined cap as per-field upper bounds while ajsm.json nulls both for the same schema gap, so the registry is INCONSISTENT on the same problem. Per-field 5/5 permits a 10-item manuscript JBJS would reject; null checks nothing at all. Rather than flip the registry's highest-profile file on my own judgement, specced a `figures_tables_combined_max` field to Sushant - strictly better than either choice, with 5+ known instances (jbjs, ajsm, asian-spine-journal, biology-of-sport, calcified-tissue-international, european-spine-journal).
